note: Literature explicitly indicates ectodermal findings in GTPBP2-related Jaberi-Elahi syndrome are age-dependent, most prominent in older individuals, and can be absent in infants under 12 months.

evidence.text: The authors observe that ectodermal manifestations and peripheral neuropathy are age-related and most prominent in older individuals with GTPBP2 biallelic variants.

source.title: Clinical delineation of GTPBP2‐associated neuro‐ectodermal syndrome: Report of two new families and review of the literature
source.quote: Our findings suggest that some aspects of the clinical presentation appear to be age-related; brain iron accumulation may appear only after childhood, and the ectodermal findings and peripheral neuropathy are most prominent in older individuals.

evidence.text: In an infant with a homozygous frameshift GTPBP2 variant, overt ectodermal manifestations were absent at 4 months of age.

source.title: A Novel Homozygous Frameshift GTPBP2 Variant in Jaberi-Elahi Syndrome: First Case Report from Türkiye
source.quote: Notably, overt ectodermal abnormalities were not evident at 4 months in our patient.
